_help: toy_harvest.py settings. Edit, then check without the robot: ~/miniconda3/envs/g1_dex3_sim2real/bin/python sim2real/harvest_moves.py (the poses, the body clearance along the scripted moves, where the hand drops into the basket). Joint vectors are the right arm in RIGHT_ARM_JOINTS order: shoulder pitch, roll, yaw, elbow, wrist roll, pitch, yaw [rad].
_home_q: HOME: the arm tucked down by the hip, nothing in front of the chest (the hand 0.30 m from the waist axis; the old home 0.46 m). The waist only turns with the arm here; the camera looks from here. Body cover clearance +4.8 cm at every waist yaw of the scan.
_ready_q: READY: where the arm-pose policy starts and ends (null = reach_io's HOME_Q, the old home the policy ran from on the robot). HOME <-> READY is a scripted joint move through home_ready_via. In sim (scripts/eval_harvest_home.py) the policy started from HOME itself brushed the hip.
_home_ready_via: the arm out to the side on the way between HOME and READY (the straight joint line cuts the thigh's cover by 5.6 cm; through here +3.7 cm worst over the scan's waist yaws)

basket._help: WHERE THE BASKET IS: from_shoulder_m = the basket point minus the right shoulder, with the waist at 0, in the torso frame [x forward, y left, z up] -- the default is the grasp pocket of the right arm stretched straight out to the right, the palm at shoulder height. It is fixed to the ground. DEPOSIT: the waist turns into waist_range_deg (only as far as needed: the nearest yaw in the range; the arm tucked at HOME; -15..0: at -30 the basket is in front and the hand went 0.31 m forward), HOME -> DEPOSIT START (beside the hip), then ONE arm-pose policy goal: the drop point (the basket point pulled toward the torso axis until it is max_reach_m from the shoulder) with the palm facing the GROUND and the fingers along the arm (the horizontal shoulder -> drop line); the hand opens (a warning if the pocket ended further than accept_m), back to DEPOSIT START -> HOME, the waist back. Sim (scripts/eval_basket_waist.py --palm down --fingers arm --no_staging): waist -30 / -15 / 0 deg 3/3 each in 3.6-4.3 s, 1.4 cm, no body overlap or near miss (the palm-horizontal drop through a staging point took 9.6-11 s). Apples within exclude_radius_m (horizontally) of the basket point are never harvested (an apple in the basket is still an apple to the camera).

moves._help: peak joint speed of the scripted moves (HOME <-> READY, HOME <-> DEPOSIT START); their safety stop on the MEASURED joint acceleration: over acc_stop_rad_s2 for acc_persist consecutive ticks, each estimated over at least acc_dt_min_s (robot 2026-10-20: one 12.4 rad/s^2 sample, the old limit 12, stopped a 0.7 rad/s^2 move with nothing wrong seen; a falling or struck arm is ~30 and lasts)

detach._help: DETACH, after the grasp and before the policy takes the apple back: the hand pulled back along its OWN approach path played backwards (the onboard runner streams the measured arm path at 25 Hz; no IK), pull_m of pocket travel at pull_speed_m_s on a quintic time scale, stiffer (kp / kd, ramped in from the policy's 100 / 10) so that a snapping stem moves the arm less. The pull eases off smoothly as kp x lead on a shoulder / elbow joint nears tau_cap_nm (the stem holds: the stored spring stays small); a joint faster than snap_dq = the stem broke: the target is put where the arm IS (the spring let go). Still holding after stall_s at the cap: the tension is let off, the hand opens (a missed try). Up to speed_stop rad/s is no safety stop while detaching, and the policy leg right after a grasp stops only above return_speed_stop (a stem letting go late; the usual stop is 1.58 rad/s: robot 2026-10-19 stopped at 1.75).

view._help: An apple is harvested only when it is whole in the head camera's picture left-right (its box at least margin_px from the left / right edges) and its centre at least edge_frac of the half-width from those edges; else the waist turns to centre it first. Above / below: no rule. image_w / fx / cx: until /unitree/color/camera_info is heard (then that); without a box (none in the message) the apple's sphere is projected with them. labels: only the detector's boxes of these classes are harvested (user 2026-10-19: red apples only; the green_apple class also fired on a person's shoes and on the cart).

waist._help: the waist counts as still (LOCKED) when its measured yaw stayed within lock_range_deg over lock_window_s, within lock_tol_deg of the target; else after lock_timeout_s the run goes on (with a warning). Robot 2026-10-19: the old speed test never passed (5 s lost at every waist move). Robot 2026-10-20: the waist settles ~1.3 deg short of its target (+11.7 for +13) -> lock_tol_deg 2.

reach._help: REACHABILITY without IK: sim2real/reach_map.py samples the arm's joint space inside the robot's limits once (offline) and stores, per 2 cm cell around the right shoulder, the palm headings that reach it (the apple's approach rule, or turned up to +-60 deg). Per apple the waist yaw (within the scan range) and the palm turn are chosen by table look-ups: the cost palm turn / palm_turn_cost_deg + waist turn / waist_turn_cost_deg is the smallest; an apple reachable at no yaw of the range is skipped. Rebuild after a change of the robot's joint limits: python3 sim2real/reach_map.py --build.

_deposit_start_q: DEPOSIT START: the arm beside the right hip (pocket 0.18 m in front of the torso, 0.33 m right; sphere-model clearance 17.6 cm), reached from HOME by a scripted joint move (body cover +5.3 cm worst); the policy goes from here to the drop and back -- not from READY, 0.33 m in front, which pushed apples (robot 2026-10-20). Sim (scripts/eval_basket_waist.py --ready_q <this> --palm down --fingers arm --no_staging): waist -30 / -15 / 0: 3/3 each, 3.4-4.8 s, no overlap, the hand at most 0.31 / 0.19 / 0.10 m in front of the torso.
_left_scan_q: LEFT ARM during the harvest (robot 2026-10-20: the left hand touched the left leg when the waist turned right): opened outward (shoulder roll +0.3), the upper arm turned so the hand points out, the elbow straighter -- 0.3 rad from the robot's rest pose [0.29, 0.22, -0.01, 0.98, 0.14, 0.01, -0.01] (body cover vs the leg -6.2 cm at waist -4); here >= +11 cm at every waist yaw -46..+16. Sent through v20's grasp_q at GO (the dual daemon passes the other arm's commands to v20), back to where it was at the end. null = the left arm not moved.

grasp_check._help: IS THE APPLE IN THE HAND: decided once the arm is back at READY after the detach -- not right after it (robot 2026-10-20: 'held' after the detach, then it fell; and an empty hand read 30 N on the thumb pad alone) -- after settle_s: the hand is in the head camera's picture there, a detector red_apple whose BOX covers the grasp pocket's pixel (FK + the detector's camera calibration, +- vision_px) with its centre within vision_m of the pocket, over vision_s = HELD, none = EMPTY (robot 2026-10-20 recordings: held -> a red_apple box at the hand; empty -> none). No detector messages: the fingers' travel decides (held between travel_min and travel_empty; camera-labelled grasps with the thumb at the picker's 30 deg: held 50-54 %, empty 65-88 %; -> 0.60; a --thumb_deg other than 30 leaves the thumb out of the travel and reads ~1.1x higher: re-check then). Back at home before the deposit the travel checks again (an apple dropped on the way: the fingers close further). The pads are only LOGGED (thumb / index / middle N; HELD by them would need 2 fingers >= held_n, EMPTY all < empty_n): unreliable on this hand. EMPTY: the hand opens, no deposit, the next apple / the scan.

reactive._help: REACTIVE FALLBACK during the APPROACH (onboard): BLOCKED when, with the palm still more than block_far_m from the apple's surface, TWO fingers' pads press >= block_n each (robot 2026-10-20: a single pad read 1.1-1.6 N on two approaches that were not blocked, and 30 N on an empty hand), or the arm lags its command beyond its gravity sag by >= block_lead_rad on a shoulder / elbow joint for block_s (real approaches 2026-10-19/20: at most 0.072 rad: the motion's own lag). The approach stops, the arm backs off; the next try comes from the side (the trunk check's free side, else one side then the other). A detach that stalls (a trunk in the hand does not come off) counts as blocked too. Thresholds not yet seen on a real trunk contact: logged.
